name: Palmetto Bay
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Palmetto Bay, FL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Palmetto Bay, FL: Light Up Your Holidays, Deering Estate holiday decor, Santa story time and a house tour with campfire.
lede: Palmetto Bay does Christmas through Village Hall and the Deering Estate: a tree lighting at Village Hall, decorated historic rooms, Santa story time and an evening house tour. Families can pair a village event with a visit to a 450 acre heritage park.
celebrates: The Village of Palmetto Bay holds its annual Light Up Your Holidays at Village Hall on East Hibiscus Street, with dance and musical performances and a 40-foot Christmas tree. Just down the road, the Deering Estate dresses the historic Richmond Cottage for the holidays and adds Santa story time, crafts and a campfire house tour in the evening. The village also lists a Community Chanukah Celebration at Village Hall, and past village messages mention a Holiday Canal Boat Parade, Holiday by the Bay and a Chabad menorah lighting among its traditions.
lastyear: In 2025 the Village of Palmetto Bay planned Light Up Your Holidays for Saturday, December 6, at Village Hall. The village calendar described dance and musical performances and a 40-foot Christmas tree lighting, and village posts also mentioned food and craft vendors and letters to Santa. At the Deering Estate, the 2025 holiday decor was themed around the Golden Age of Travel and was planned to run from November 28, 2025, through January 6, 2026, inside the Richmond Cottage.
facts: Deering Estate is one of seven Miami-Dade County Heritage Parks and covers 450 acres with eight native ecosystems. It is at 16701 SW 72nd Avenue in Palmetto Bay. Charles Deering's Navy years and love of sailing, travel and Biscayne Bay shape its holiday decor, and the estate says the Stone House is closed for renovation while the rest of the estate stays open. The Deering Estate Foundation was established in 1989, and the Census Bureau estimated the village population at 24,886 in 2025.
trains: Palmetto Bay does not have its own train station. The closest Metrorail stop is Dadeland South, at 9090 South Dixie Highway, which Miami-Dade Transit lists as the southernmost Metrorail station on the Green Line. Metrorail is the county's elevated train, and families can pair a ride with a Santa visit at Dadeland Mall. For rail cars and small train rides, the Gold Coast Railroad Museum is at 12450 SW 152nd Street in Miami.
train_links: Train rides, rail cars and a model train building at 12450 SW 152nd Street in Miami.
traditions: The village's annual Village Hall event features dance and musical performances and the lighting of a 40-foot Christmas tree.
Historic holiday decor at Deering Estate
Rooms in the Richmond Cottage are decorated by community groups, with a theme that changes each year.
Story time and photos with Santa
The Deering Estate hosts story time with Santa's elves and a photo with Santa inside the historic Richmond Cottage.
The Deering Estate opens in the evening for guided house tours and a campfire.
The village lists a Chanukah celebration at Village Hall during the holiday season.
Past village messages list a Holiday Canal Boat Parade among Palmetto Bay's community traditions.
kidfact: The Deering Estate has eight different native ecosystems on its 450 acres, so kids can spot very different plants and animals in one park.
faq: Where is the Palmetto Bay tree lighting?

The Village of Palmetto Bay holds Light Up Your Holidays at Village Hall, 9705 E. Hibiscus Street. The village calendar says the event features dance and musical performances, a 40-foot Christmas tree lighting and more, and thanks local parking sponsors. Check the village calendar for the current year's date and time before you go.
Is the Deering Estate in Palmetto Bay?

Yes. The Deering Estate is at 16701 SW 72nd Avenue, Palmetto Bay, FL 33157. Miami-Dade County lists it as one of seven Heritage Parks. It runs several holiday events, including decorated historic rooms, Santa story time and an evening house tour, and each has its own admission price.
What is Tides and Tidings at Deering Estate?

Tides and Tidings is the estate's holiday decor theme, inspired by Charles Deering's love of the sea and Biscayne Bay. The Richmond Cottage is decorated with nautical and coastal touches, and community groups and volunteers help decorate rooms. It is included with general admission, and children under 4 are free.
Does Palmetto Bay have a Hanukkah celebration?

Yes. The Village of Palmetto Bay lists a Community Chanukah Celebration at Village Hall on its parks and recreation calendar. Past village agendas also list a menorah lighting celebration at Village Hall, so the village has marked Hanukkah alongside Christmas events in recent years.
How do we get to Palmetto Bay without a car?

The closest Metrorail station is Dadeland South, at 9090 South Dixie Highway, the southernmost stop on the Green Line. Miami-Dade Transit runs buses from there, so families should check the county's trip planner for the route to the Village Hall or the Deering Estate.
